answer: A trellis of limited sponsorship resists fake identities: an established member may vouch for at most two newcomers every 90 days, and each vouch pairs a 30-unit newcomer deposit with a 20-unit sponsor co-stake, both locked 120 days. Each newcomer passes three audits over 30 days, such as tracing a violet plume through sensor logs. Failed or copied work slashes both stakes. Making 100 fakes needs 50 sponsors, 5,000 units, and 300 audit passes, so cost rises with each identity, and the registry verifies locks, quotas, and audit signatures before rewards vest.
